text:
sam: Heads-up — customer success flagged a bunch of trial accounts hammering inference with tiny prompts + high concurrency. They behave like normal apps but spawn thousands of short-lived probes. Looking for design follow-up: do we treat trial bursts as normal tenant load or special-case them with a different admission pipeline?
maria: Can you paste an example? is this the same fingerprint pattern as last month?
sam: example: 50 reqs/s from ~200 distinct API keys, each request 3-8 tokens of prompt, 1-2 tokens of completion. No auth abuse detected, keys are freshly minted trial keys. Patterns: high connection churn, lots of parallel streams, TCP sessions short.
kai: Two obvious options: 1) hard quota for trials (simple) 2) per-key token bucket with aggressive decay + cross-key correlation for the same IP/fingerprint (more complex). Hard quotas are simple but bad UX for legitimate power users on trial.
linda: UX concern + sales impact. We should prefer soft controls first: probablistic admission + preferencing for paying customers. Could do a "trial credit reservoir" per-account that fills slowly and drains quickly on bursts.
sam: Agree. Also we need to prevent tokenless probes that try to stay under per-key thresholds by rotating keys. So correlation needs to include device/IP/agent string + subtle features (entropy of prompts, inter-arrival distribution). We should be careful about PII.
maria: For privacy: use hashed fingerprints + k-anonymity thresholds. Only escalate when group size > N to avoid targeting single user.
kai: On implementation: we can extend the admission service to support a two-tier policy: admission_policy { allowed_rate, burst_cost, credit_pool_id } and a separate correlation service that maps ephemeral keys to credit_pool_id based on stable fingerprint. Pseudoconfig: 
```
admission_policy: {
  type: "trial",
  allowed_rate: 5,        # reqs/s per key baseline
  burst_cost: 10,         # tokens deducted from pool per burst
  credit_pool: "trial_pool_v1"
}
```
This keeps runtime checks fast while offloading heavier correlation to a background scorer.
linda: We need telemetry: attribute dropped requests to "soft-shed" vs "hard-deny" and surface in Console for Sales. Add a trace tag like `abuse_mitigation.reason` and `fingerprint.group_id`.
rate-bot: Detect: trial-burst spike 2026-02-14T16:23:00Z, affected_keys=214, peak_rps=320, avg_latency +12ms on p99.
maria: Tradeoffs: correlation reduces false positives but increases state and potentially latency if we consult extra services. We must ensure admission remains local for SLO. Proposal: make admission decision in two phases: quick stateless check (local token bucket) -> allow/soft-shed -> async enrichment (background scorer) -> if enrichment signals abuse, schedule retroactive penalties and notify CS.
kai: Retroactive penalties are risky (billing chargebacks). Better: record and only throttle future requests and surface to ops; don't change past billing.
sam: Also consider probabilistic early rejection: for load spikes above cluster capacity, randomly drop a fraction of requests from trial pools with a tunable seed per region so behavior is reproducible for debugging.
linda: We should add a canary rollout for the new pipeline: 1) start with detection-only mode, 2) enable soft-shed for top-10% offending clusters, 3) expand to full rollout after 2 weeks of metrics.
maria: Add eval prompt set to monitor false positives: a few known legitimate trial apps we whitelist for testing.
kai: Ops change: admission service config must be dynamic via config-server, and correlation models hot-swappable via feature flags. Also export per-pool metrics: credits_left, avg_burst_cost, soft_shed_rate.
sam: Any objections to prototype in eng-staging next week? I'll own the spike tests and synthetic workload.
linda: +1 from CS side, but add rollback hooks and an auto-open ticket to CS when a customer loses access due to soft-shed.
maria: I'll draft an RFC describing: credit pools, correlation constraints (privacy-safe), two-phase admission, telemetry schema, and rollout plan. Target EOD Fri.
sam: Great — thanks. I'll post synthetic load scripts and sample traces in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
